newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks expected to open mixed to lower.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks expected to open mixed to lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to trade mixed to lower at the opening Monday after the second biggest point loss ever on Friday amid fears that corporate America's future profits may lose some of their luster.
The dollar, whose further slide Friday against the mark also contributed to the Dow's slide, was stabler in overnight trading.
"We may see a mixed opening with mild downside pressure," said Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
"On balance we ought to have a decidedly better day than Friday. We may see a bit of bargain hunting mixed with an attempt at stabilization," Ackerman added.
U.S. blue chips dipped in overnight trading in London.
But traders noted that the long bond's tone was firmer, up 1/32 to yield 6.55 percent, and the S&P 500 Futures were also higher, up 3.70 points at 902.50 just after 0800 EDT/1200 GMT.

No major economic news was due Monday. The Federal Open Market Committee meets in Washington Tuesday but analysts said they did not expect the Fed to hike interest rates following last week's slew of benign inflation data.
But news before the bell that Hewlett-Packard's third quarter results were below analysts' expectations could compound the key tech stock sector's woes.
Dealers said Hewlett was down over three at about 63. The stock closed at 66-3/16 on Friday.
Several technology stocks moved lower in overnight trading in London.
The Dow was rattled Friday by a profit warning from blue chip Gillette, just a week after Coca-Cola Co said its earnings might not fall in line with analysts' expectations.
In Asia the dollar was driven down from a high of 118.05 yen on comments by a U.S. trade official, but some support was noted. The dollar was trading at 117.34/44.
In Europe, the dollar was able to recover from overnight session lows. The dollar was trading at 1.8188/98 marks.
Japan's Nikkei 225 index closed down 284.93 points or 1.47 percent at 19,041.10.
In London the FTSE 100 was off 28.7 points or 0.59 percent at 4837.1.

The Wall Street Journal in its "Heard on the Street" column said some investors now think the Nifty 50, the small group of powerful multinationals, is finally set to cede market dominance to a broader group of stocks.
